items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: It's a nostalgic theme and it's -- and it's like Tommy Dorsey playing -- everyone wants to play it exactly like they play it.

ctx.x: Yes. There was much improvising. And a lot of times -- you know -- guys would take something somebody else had played they'd heard played -- you know -- put it in there. It's like they used to play a regular trombone solo on -- they thought it was a really great thing to do you know. Play it -- sing on the road.

And if it was a masterpiece thing -- everyone wants to play it today -- they try to play (singing) -- but you know invariably they'd want to play his solo. Everybody -- you know -- but it's (inaudible) they're playing really. It's a nostalgic theme and it's -- and it's like Tommy Dorsey playing -- everyone wants to play it exactly like they play it.
That's the way it was in those days, too. You hear somebody playing something and you know -- copy it. They'd help them around like that a good deal.
